To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) DT and its derivatives are widely used in biomedical research, and in some cases, they have a therapeutic effect; (2) the main biological functions of DT are associated with the ability to enter the cell, to inhibit the protein synthesis and to kill the cell; (3) the main target of DT is the elongation factor 2; (4) the biological properties of the DT derivatives are mainly associated with the presence of the catalytic and translocation domains.
the DT and its derivatives have a number of important biological functions.

DT derivatives are used for the study of DT biological properties, for construction of the new recombinant vaccines, for the creation of gene transfer vectors, for the development of new methods of cancer treatment and for the construction of the new biotechnology tools.
In summary, our research is concerned with
studying the properties of recombinant DT derivatives and their medical application.
the development of new methods of treatment and prevention of various types of cancer, as well as with the study of the mechanisms of action of antitumor drugs.
the study of biological properties and medical application of diphtheria toxins and their derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recombinant derivatives have become a powerful and irreplaceable tool for studying DT and DT-mediated biological processes.
recombinant derivatives and analogs of DT have been used for a long time and are widely used in modern biological and medical researches.
recombinant analogues of DT are very useful tools for biomedical research as well as for biotechnological applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the derivatives of DT have a wide spectrum of biological activity and medical application.
the DT and its fragments are the powerful and multifunctional tools in the modern biomedical research.

the derivatives of diphtheria toxins are used for the following purposes: • as a model for the study of the molecular mechanism of the action of the toxins of other bacterial pathogens; • as an effective tool for the targeted delivery of various molecules (drugs, genes, etc.) into the cytosol of cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombinant DNA techniques allow obtaining the derivatives of DT, which are much more useful for biomedical research than natural mutants of the toxin.
the recombinant derivatives are the most important tool for studying the biological and medical properties of DT.
DT derivatives can be used for a wide range of medical and biomedical purposes, from the development of new drugs to the study of the mechanisms of action of native toxin.
